result.process_description:
Title: Farming Bot

Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.

result.rule: Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Each lane flowNodeRef identifies a node in the owning process. Assign nodes according to stated responsibility and avoid arbitrary membership.
Model performer information only when responsibility is stated. Prefer lanes for ordinary organizational responsibility.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

result.rule: When the description says that after a participant has supplied all of their choices, a separate automated actor acting for that participant starts its work, and the description names no further participant action between the last choice and that start: Connect the last choice task in the participant's lane directly to the start of the automated actor's work in that actor's own lane. Do not add a confirmation or review task in the participant's lane that the description does not state, and do not place the automated actor's start, ongoing work, or checks in the participant's lane.

When the description names one actor who selects or supplies choices and a separate automated actor that carries out the work after those choices are complete, and both act within the same process: Wrap the whole process in one bpmn:participant pool, and model each named actor as its own lane inside that pool. Place the activities the human actor performs (choosing, prioritizing, supplying inputs) and the process start in the human actor's lane. Place the automated work that runs after all choices are collected in the automated actor's lane. Do not leave the automated actor's activities in the human actor's lane, and do not omit the pool or lanes.

When the description says a participant may perform an action at any time while an ongoing activity of that same participant is running (for example, updating a list during an activity that is still in progress): Model the action as a flow node inside the same process as the participant's lane that holds the ongoing activity. Have that lane reference the node, and connect the node to the ongoing activity's scope so it can occur during that activity. Do not place the action's start or any of its nodes in a separate process or pool, and do not have a lane reference a node that is not defined in its own process.

When the description states that a role takes a decision on whether one or more optional activities are needed, the activities that follow are performed by other roles and may occur together, and they then converge before a later step performed by a role: Model the split as an inclusive gateway placed in the lane of the role that takes the decision, and do not leave it out of the model. Put the conditional activities each in the lane of their performing role, with one flow from the split to each activity labeled with its stated condition. Close them with a matching inclusive join placed in the lane of the role responsible for the step that follows, and connect that join to the next step. Do not move the split or the join into the lane of a role that does not take or carry out that step.
